title: A job step that calls a cataloged procedure and overrides its PARM, COND and a DD by procedure step name
shapes: BDLD jcl/BDLDOVR.jcl: //RPT020.RPTOUT DD SYSOUT=B after the EXEC, replacing the procedure's RPTOUT
asserts: The calling EXEC is one jcl_steps fact (step QTR, exec_proc BDLDPRC) carrying parm_overrides [{step RPT020, parm QUARTERLY}] and cond_overrides [{step RPT020, cond (4,LT,SRT010)}]; its own parm and cond are null. The overriding DD is a jcl_dds fact of step QTR with dd RPTOUT, override_of RPT020 and sysout B; the procedure's own RPTOUT (sysout A, in BDLDPRC) is unchanged. The PARM actually passed to BDLDRPT at run time is QUARTERLY, not the symbolic default.

citations.section: Modifying Procedures > Coding an overriding OUTPUT JCL or DD statement
citations.quote: the name of the procedure step containing the overridden statement, followed by a period, followed by the name of the procedure OUTPUT JCL statement or the ddname of the procedure DD statement.

citations.section: EXEC statement > PARM parameter > On an EXEC statement that calls a procedure
citations.quote: The EXEC statement can have as many PARM.procstepname parameters as the procedure has steps; each PARM parameter must specify a unique procstepname.

citations.section: EXEC statement > COND parameter > On an EXEC statement that calls a procedure
citations.quote: The EXEC statement can have as many COND.procstepname parameters as the procedure has steps; each COND parameter must specify a unique procstepname.
